A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from WallFacer to StarTrail. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendix material support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated in v4.

before.justification: v3 Section 4 reports original throughput, GPU-memory, and strong- and weak-scaling measurements for GPT and DiT models on A100/H100 clusters.

after.justification: v4 retains these original measurements in Section 4, with the supported-sequence-length comparison relocated to Appendix B.

M1.justification: v4 removes the automatic topology-scheduler component documented in v3 Section 3.4, including grid search over team size and communication placement. The core QKV replication, sub-ring attention, and initialization algorithms remain; the renamed system does not introduce a new attention procedure.

E1.justification: The reported coverage remains GPT/DiT long-sequence training, causal/full attention, and A100/H100 environments. The 3B/7B/13B sequence-length feasibility table in v4 Appendix B is retained from v3 Table 4. Larger batches and models receive discussion, not additional evaluation.

E2.justification: Ring Attention remains the evaluated comparator in the throughput, memory, scaling, and sequence-length comparisons. The newly cited USP work is not added as an experimental baseline.

E3.justification: v4 Table 1 replaces v3 Table 2's duplicated 16-GPUs-by-2-nodes A100 entry with 4 GPUs by 8 nodes. v4 Section 4.3 also describes weak scaling as 8–32 GPUs, although its retained GPT plot includes 64. These are revisions to reported settings; they do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The C=2/C=4 comparisons, hardware-adaptability and scaling analyses, and ZigZag load-balancing illustration are retained. Relocating material into appendices does not add analyses, and Appendix B.2's larger-batch/model argument is not a new ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: v4 Checklist item 7 newly discloses averaging measurements over a large number of training iterations and explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical-significance reporting. It supplies no iteration count, seeds, error bars, or confidence intervals and does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: Figures 7–10 and the sequence-length table retain their results. v4 adds Figure 1 throughput panels without sufficient settings to match all values. Section 4.2 changes Ring using 7.9–30.79% less memory into StarTrail using 7.9–30.79% more and drops the DiT 512K/C=4 exception despite unchanged Figure 8. These percentages are not equivalent.

T1.justification: Section 3.2.2 revises communication-round counts from P and P/C² to P−1 and P/C²−1, changing both bandwidth and latency terms. The memory formulas remain equivalent, while v3's formal grid-search selection rule, Equation 8, is removed.

C1.justification: The central efficiency and scalability claims, including the 77.12% GPT and 114.33% DiT headline gains, remain. v4 drops the explicit automatic configuration-search contribution and more clearly frames its contribution as optimizing ring-style parallelism alongside orthogonal head-sharding methods.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 adds an argument for generalizing small-batch/model measurements to larger settings. Section 4.3 and the conclusion add explicit ring-scalability and hybrid-co-design limitations. The earlier topology-specific explanation of optimal C and detailed weak-scaling rationale are removed.

D1.justification: v4 specifies H100 inter-node bandwidth as 8×400 Gbps and newly states that code is not publicly available. It removes v3's peak-allocated-memory measurement description and sequence-length control for avoiding cuda_free overhead. Most runtime and initialization details are retained in Appendix A.

R1.justification: v4 adds Fang and Zhao's USP citation and emphasizes complementary head-sharding/ring approaches. It removes the n-body inspiration and Driscoll/Hockney references, together with Reformer and online-normalizer background citations. Most remaining related work is retained or relocated to Appendix B.3.

P1.justification: The paper undergoes extensive condensation and reorganization alongside the WallFacer-to-StarTrail rename. Background and motivation are reorganized, attention receives a new three-phase explanation, and substantial technical, discussion, and related-work material moves into appendices. A checklist and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: The two-column document becomes single-column with extensive figure and table relocation. Figure 1 gains throughput panels, Figure 3 is substantially revised with a concentric-ring illustration, cluster/model tables are merged, and initialization algorithms, the load-balancing figure, and sequence-length table move into appendices.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the method explanation and diagrams, but weakens reporting of the central memory tradeoff. Section 4.2 reverses v3's percentage baseline without recalculation: 30.79% less corresponds to about 44.49% more. It also drops the DiT 512K exception still visible in Figure 8 and removes memory-measurement controls. Revised communication equations retain numerical examples based on the earlier formulas. These limited accuracy and reproducibility losses outweigh the expository gains.
